correctness.rationale: An independent graph-inequality enumeration constructs the facets from coordinate and independent-set neighborhood inequalities and checks completeness by dual level sets: a negative t-level set of a weight vector nonnegative on edges is independent, and its neighbors belong to the positive t-level set. This reconstructs the full lattice, all twelve facet supports and 153 nonempty faces, and every primitive active normal. Exact ranks and minor gcds give (10,25,10) singular orbits with no higher-dimensional singular orbits and no simplicial singularities. Inclusion-maximal singular faces give exactly the five listed primitive edges and ten unimodular triangles, hence the stated lines and planes. The proof prose reverses the wrong ordering in one sentence: it is normal cones that reverse face inclusion; orbit closures preserve polytope face inclusion. The maximal-face computation and Finding use the correct order. At each maximal face the rays generate the full transverse lattice; their relation has sign group sizes 2 and 2, or 2 and 3 respectively, with unit coefficients. The dual semigroup consists of nonnegative integer entries of equal group sum and is generated by all cross-group pairs. Swapping partners via 2x2 minors connects all products with the same group totals, giving precisely the two rank-one matrix cone rings as stated; the argument is characteristic-independent. Non-Q-factoriality is exactly nonsimpliciality here.
residual_risks: The statement is about the normal-fan model and reduced support. It does not give singular scheme structure or transverse germs at intersections.

evidence: The irredundant prior facet system consists of rim coordinates, the two sum bounds for odd rim length and inequalities from maximal rim-independent sets. Specializing to n=5 gives exactly 5+2+5 facets. Its fixed-chart proof analyzes the active normal vectors at spokes to derive the class group and canonical Cartier condition.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior inequalities implicitly determine the entire normal fan. To infer the audited support and generic local types from them still requires identifying the active ray sets at nonvertices, checking the simplicial lattice indices at every face, and classifying the maximal nonsmooth cones by their saturated relations. The fixed-point class-group calculation itself does not perform or imply that classification.

value.rationale: The first odd wheel beyond the four-vertex rim is a natural test object in the ordinary wheel family. The complete positive-dimensional singular strata demonstrate non-equidimensional reduced singular support and two different generic local toric models within the same fivefold. That makes the exact classification useful as a benchmark for toric singular-support computations, beyond re-enumerating the known wheel facets or fixed charts.
residual_risks: No general classification of wheel singular supports or claims about resolution geometry follow here.
